Summary and read-through with Beige Book and SLOOS context

- Policy stance: FOMC held the target range at 4.25–4.50% (IORB 4.4%, ON RRP 4.25%) and will continue modest QT with existing caps. Guidance remains explicitly data dependent with balanced risk language. Two dissents favored a 25 bp cut, signaling an emerging easing bias if inflation cools further.
- Macro backdrop: Statement notes moderated growth in H1, low unemployment with solid labor conditions, and inflation “somewhat elevated,” alongside elevated uncertainty.
- Beige Book cross-check: District reports point to flat-to-slight growth, mixed consumer spending with softer discretionary outlays, soft manufacturing, and more normalizing labor markets (easier hiring, lower churn, slower wage growth). Price increases continue to moderate but remain above 2% in many categories. Credit conditions remain tight, and CRE—especially office—shows ongoing weakness with higher vacancies and financing headwinds.
- SLOOS lens: Banks report tighter-than-average lending standards and subdued loan demand across C&I (especially for smaller/below-IG firms), CRE, and consumer credit (autos, cards), with weak mortgage/HELOC demand. This implies continued drag on private demand and heightened sensitivity for small firms and riskier borrowers.
- Implications: Beige Book and SLOOS together reinforce the cautious hold. They tilt risks slightly to the downside for growth via tighter credit and CRE stress, while easing labor/price pressures support a gradual shift toward easing if inflation continues to cool. The dovish dissents underscore this potential path but are tempered by ongoing uncertainty.

Net effect on tone
- Compared with a SLOOS-only read, the Beige Book’s confirmation of tepid demand, ongoing CRE stress, and tighter credit nudges the tone modestly more negative despite an emerging easing bias.
